title: Normalized sf/PBC heart and continuous finite-stage model
statement:
Fix $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$ and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. For every separated finite-type $k$-scheme $W$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] and finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Omega$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], use the sf raw category, its standard halves [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure], the PBC raw category with its standard halves [prop-weil-localized-tstructure], and their common-stage categories [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients; def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. Put $A=\mathcal O_E$, choose $\varpi=\varpi_E$, and put $B_{E,W}=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/\varpi^n)_W$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $J_{W,E}$ and $J_W$ be the identity-induced equivalences of [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison], and let $\mathcal R_{W,E}$ be the PBC continuous realization of [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization].

Every such $W$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], has finite Krull dimension [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], and has $\ell$ invertible. These equivalences identify the sf and PBC standard halves in every degree, integrally, at $E$, and at $\Omega$. Integrally both categories are the same full subcategory of $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_{E,W}))$ with the same ambient cohomology sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization; prop-weil-pbc-integral-tstructure]; both nonpositive halves are defined by vanishing above zero and both nonnegative halves by vanishing below zero. At $E$ their halves are the isomorphism closures of the same integral halves, and at $\Omega$ their halves are the isomorphism closures of the same finite-stage halves. In particular, for every $M$ in the sf common-stage heart there are one finite $E$ and $M_E$ in the sf $E$-heart with $(E,M_E)\cong M$. For this choice $\mathcal R_{W,E}J_{W,E}M_E$ is a constructible $B_{E,W}[1/\varpi]$-module sheaf $F$ in degree zero. Constructible means that $F$ is pro-etale locally finite free on the members of a finite locally closed partition, with finite ranks allowed to vary [def-constructible-stratification]. No degree-zero assertion is imposed on an arbitrary integral representative of $M_E$.

For every morphism $h:V\to W$ of such schemes, not necessarily $k$-linear, there is a natural isomorphism of functors in the raw derived categories
$$J_{V,E}Lh^{*,\mathrm{sf}}_E\cong Lh^{*,\mathrm{pbc}}_EJ_{W,E},$$
for the completed pullbacks of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom; def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Its integral normalization is the identity of the entire finite-reduction pullback diagram: all reductions come from the same flat-term K-flat representative, with the actual quotient transitions. Its rationalization and common-stage extension respect identities, composition, finite coefficient extension and its associators, with the whole-diagram realization comparisons of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. Under $\mathcal R$ this is the ordinary derived module inverse image; for a locally closed immersion it is exact ordinary inverse image. Thus the isomorphism carrying $M_E$ to $F$ restricts compatibly along any finite succession of locally closed immersions. All these assertions include empty schemes and zero objects.

source.place: Section 6.8, Proposition 6.8.14(2) and Remark 6.8.15; agent comparison of the sf/PBC standard halves and whole completed pullback diagrams, expanded from old item steps 1-3 and blueprint paragraph 6.

proof.text: The hypotheses needed for all the comparison inputs hold for $W$ and likewise for every $V$. A field is Noetherian: its only ideals are zero and the whole ring; its spectrum has a one-element affine cover. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to $W\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its dimension is finite by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. Since $k$ has characteristic $p$ and $\ell\ne p$, the nonzero scalar $\ell$ has an inverse in $k$; its image is a unit in every local ring of $W$. None of these arguments requires $W$ to be nonempty.

source.place: Section 6.8, hypotheses on schemes; verification for the present finite-type schemes is an agent argument.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]: the sf and PBC integral categories are the identical full subcategory of the same $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_{E,W}))$, with the same reductions. The sf half-definition [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure] and the PBC half-description [prop-weil-pbc-integral-tstructure] both test the same ambient $\mathcal H^r$. The identity therefore preserves and reflects each half. Applying the same observation to $K[m]$ proves the assertion in degree $m$, since the inherited shifts agree.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), and the sf/PBC integral half-definitions; agent identity comparison.

proof.text: By [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison], $J_{W,E}$ is induced by this integral identity, on objects and localized arrows. The sf rational halves in [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure] and the PBC halves in [prop-weil-localized-tstructure] are the isomorphism closures of the images of the respective integral halves. Thus an integral half-witness and its rational isomorphism give a half-witness under $J_{W,E}$; its inverse works identically. At the common stage, $J_W(E,K)=(E,J_{W,E}K)$ with the coherent scalar comparisons specified in the same comparison lemma. The common-stage halves, defined by finite-stage witnesses, are consequently identified in both directions and every degree as well.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2); passage to the common finite-stage categories is the agent comparison of their definitions.

proof.text: To obtain a representative in both halves at once, choose $M\cong(E_1,U)$ with $U\in D^{\le0}_c(W,E_1)$ and $M\cong(E_2,V)$ with $V\in D^{\ge0}_c(W,E_2)$, using [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure]. Represent the resulting isomorphism $(E_1,U)\cong(E_2,V)$ and its inverse over a common finite field. The Hom-colimit equality rule of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] puts their two inverse identities over one further finite $E$. Their representatives then give an actual isomorphism $U_E\cong V_E$. Scalar extension preserves both halves: its commutation with canonical truncations and their maps in [prop-constructible-truncations] sends a zero complementary truncation to zero. Thus $M_E=U_E$ lies in the nonpositive half and, being isomorphic to $V_E$, also in the nonnegative half. Its common-stage image is isomorphic to $M$. This uses only finitely many arrows and equalities; it assumes neither that stage inclusions reflect halves nor that an arbitrary integral representative is in the integral heart.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14, finite coefficient descent; explicit agent argument from the common-stage Hom definition.

proof.text: The preceding half-identification puts $J_{W,E}M_E$ in the PBC rational heart. Apply [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization]: its t-exact realization identifies precisely that heart with the constructible $B_{E,W}[1/\varpi]$-module sheaves in degree zero. Let $F$ be its image in that heart, with the resulting derived isomorphism $\mathcal R_{W,E}J_{W,E}M_E\cong F[0]$. The meaning of constructible, including a finite locally closed partition and varying finite ranks, is exactly the one in that lemma. This conclusion concerns the localized object and makes no assertion about the other cohomology of an integral representative.

For any scheme map $h:V\to W$, choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P\to K$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The definitions [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom; def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] use the reductions $P_n=P\otimes_{B_{E,W}}(A/\varpi^n)_W$ and their quotient transitions. Keep the coefficient-presentation identification explicit: [def-pur-completed-coefficient-presentation-transport] identifies the completed rings with their finite projections and defines $\Phi$ with round trips equal to the identity on module sections. Under step 2's common integral category, its inverse is the integral identity inducing the fixed $J_{W,E}$ of [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison]. Apply (1) of [lem-pur-framework-pbc-pullback-scalar-bridge] to this presentation equivalence. It supplies $\pi_{h,E}$ as realization of the identity of the entire strict tower $\operatorname{Res}_nh_n^*P_n$, with actual transitions and every projection preserved. This gives the integral comparison naturally, including its specified identity and composition comparisons. The schemes meet the bridge's Noetherian, finite-dimension and invertibility hypotheses by step 1; it assumes neither that $h$ is an isomorphism nor that it is $k$-linear.

source.place: Tag 099N, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case (2),(5); current framework/PBC bridge clauses (1),(2),(4) and completed coefficient presentation normalization; agent assembly.

proof.text: Localize $\pi_{h,E}$ of step 6 on arrows: $f/\varpi^n$ receives the integral comparison of $f$ multiplied by $\varpi^{-n}$. This is the fixed $J$ action in [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison], so it gives the displayed rational natural isomorphism. To check its scalar normalization, use (2) of [lem-pur-framework-pbc-pullback-scalar-bridge]: the PBC map is $p_h=(\widehat\delta_h)^{-1}:C_VF^{\mathrm{pbc}}_{h,E}\to F^{\mathrm{pbc}}_{h,L}C_W$, and its $j$ is the inverse of the specified completion map followed by coefficient relabeling. Its displayed square identifies this $p_h$ with the framework comparison $a_h$ under $\pi$ and $j$. Thus the comparison uses the prescribed PBC scalar map in its corrected direction. Clause (1) identifies the specified compositors, and (4) gives shifts, identities, successive-extension associators and raw rationalization. These are compatible with the whole-diagram framework normalization in [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. For a common-stage arrow, conjugate its finite-stage representative by the fixed $j$ maps of [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison]. The bridge's square makes the resulting arrow agree with either pullback route. Its identity and successive-extension equations imply independence of further enlargement; intermediate comparison maps cancel for composites. Hence the common-stage extension respects the fixed scalar associators and all finite compositions.

source.place: Tag 099N, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case (2),(5); current framework/PBC bridge clauses (1),(2),(4), in particular the corrected direction p_h=(widehat delta_h)^{-1}; agent raw rationalization and common-stage descent.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization] to the PBC side of the step-7 comparison. For every $h$ it identifies that pullback with $B_{E,V}[1/\varpi]\otimes^L_{h^{-1}(B_{E,W}[1/\varpi])}h^{-1}(-)$. For a locally closed immersion its coefficient map is an isomorphism and this functor is exact ordinary inverse image, by the same lemma. Apply it to the isomorphism in step 5. This gives the isomorphism on the restricted object and on its degree-zero sheaf. The identity/composition and coefficient compatibilities of that lemma and step 7 show that, along two immersions, the iterated isomorphism is the one for the composite after the specified composition comparison. Induction on the length of a finite succession gives the claimed compatibility for every such succession, including length zero.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; identity, composition and coefficient normalizations as in the continuous realization lemma.

proof.text: All constructions used zero-preserving functors and isomorphism-closed halves, so they also apply to the zero object. On the empty scheme every sheaf of modules is zero by its sheaf condition for the empty covering; the empty partition witnesses constructibility. The same tower, comparison and inverse-image formulas therefore prove all clauses there, with no separate nonzero rank or nonempty stratum assumption.

source.place: Definitions and the empty-cover sheaf condition; agent edge-case verification.
